issues.failure_explanation: The asymptotic formula G(∞)=(C+D)/(C-D/2) is only valid when C≠D/2 and is used to conclude that C+D=0 forces G(∞)=0. For C=D=0 (which satisfies C+D=0) the denominator of G reduces to 1-z/6 and the numerator to 1+z(1/6+2R(z)/3), so G(z)→(5/6)/(-1/6)=-5 as z→∞. Thus the 'if' direction of the lemma is false at C=D=0; it holds only for C+D=0 with C≠0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis C≠0 (equivalently C≠D/2) to the 'if' direction and note the leading-order cancellation argument for C+D=0, C≠0.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma as stated is false in one degenerate case; the parameter range used later (C∈[0.018824,0.045589]) excludes C=0, so downstream use is unaffected.
issues.title: Lemma 3.1 'if' direction fails in the degenerate case C=D=0 (G(∞)=-5, not 0)
issues.why_classification: A local hypothesis fixing a degenerate case; all substantive claims survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed Re(z)=(1/3+13C)/(6C) is the real part of the roots only when the discriminant (1/3+13C)^2-24C is negative. For every C<0 the discriminant 169C^2-46C/3+1/9 is positive, so both roots of \eqref{equation_C} are real with product 2/(3C)<0; one root is negative, i.e. a pole of G lies in the left half-plane. Hence for C<-1/39 (e.g. C=-1: root (38/3-\sqrt{(38/3)^2+24})/6<0) G is not analytic in Re(z)≤0, contradicting the lemma. The correct statement is analyticity iff C≥0 (for C>0 both roots have positive product and positive sum).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the lemma as 'iff C≥0' and prove it by treating the real-root case via the sign of the product and sum of the roots (Vieta), instead of the averaged real-part formula.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.2 is false on the branch C<-1/39; the later A-stability range lies in C>0, so the final scheme is unaffected, but the stated characterization of Condition 1 must be withdrawn for negative C.
issues.title: Lemma 3.2 wrongly asserts analyticity for C<-1/39; real-part formula assumes complex roots
issues.why_classification: The correction is short but necessarily removes a claimed parameter region from the lemma; the downstream A-stability result is preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Analytically proving $\lvert G(iy)\lvert\leq 1$ for all $y\in\mathbb{R}$ is complex. Instead, we employ a systematic numerical scanning algorithm

issues.failure_explanation: Writing G=P/Q with P(z)=q_1(1+\alpha z)+\beta z p_1-Cz^3/2, Q(z)=(1-az+bz^2)q_1 (q_1=1-z/4+z^2/48, p_1=1+z/4+z^2/48, \alpha=1/6+7C/2, \beta=2/3-10C, a=1/6+13C/2, b=3C/2), one gets exactly |Q(iy)|^2-|P(iy)|^2 = E_6 y^6 + (C^2/1024) y^8 with E_6=(-1+75C-1170C^2)/3456 (the y^2 and y^4 coefficients vanish by fourth order). Hence |G(iy)|≤1 for all y iff 1170C^2-75C+1≤0, i.e. C∈[(75-\sqrt{945})/2340,(75+\sqrt{945})/2340]≈[0.018914,0.045188]. At the paper's endpoints C=0.018824 and C=0.045589 one has E_6<0, so |G(iy)|>1 for 0<y≲1.5 (e.g. |G(i)|≈1+2·10^{-7} at C=0.018824, ≈1+8·10^{-7} at C=0.045589): the scheme is not A-stable there. The stated interval is therefore false, and the conclusion is in any case asserted without proof (numerical scan only). The 'optimal damping' claim for C=0.018924 is likewise unsupported (near the lower boundary E_6≈0, so damping on the imaginary axis is minimal).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the interval by the exact E-polynomial condition 1170C^2-75C+1≤0 (C≈[0.018914,0.045188]) and prove Condition 2 analytically via |Q(iy)|^2-|P(iy)|^2=E_6y^6+C^2y^8/1024≥0; drop or justify the optimality statement.
issues.overall_effect: Conclusion 3.3 and the final scheme \eqref{stage_1_final}-\eqref{Stage_2_final} advertise A-stability for a parameter range that includes non-A-stable values; the guarantee 'A-stable for all C in [0.018824,0.045589]' is false and the optimality claim is unsupported.
issues.title: Claimed A-stability interval for C is incorrect at its ends and rests only on numerical scanning
issues.why_classification: A contained analytic argument (E-polynomial) yields a comparable, slightly narrower interval; the A-stability result survives but the stated range and its numerical justification must be replaced.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: focusing on stable time step size and convergence error, to verify the superiority of the former
demonstrate that the proposed scheme possesses superior stability regions and smaller numerical errors

issues.failure_explanation: The paper promises a comparison of stable time step sizes, but every table lists both methods converging at every step tested and no stability limit, stability region, or failed step is reported for either method; only errors are compared. The classical fourth-order implicit RK (Gauss) is itself A-stable, so no step-size restriction distinguishes the two methods on the test problems, and 'superior stability regions' is not established anywhere in the source.

failure_location.quote: offers superior stability that enables even larger step sizes

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claims to the demonstrated smaller errors (and the L-stability-type property G(∞)=0 versus |R(∞)|=1 for Gauss RK), or add experiments exhibiting a stability/step-size advantage.
issues.overall_effect: The comparative stability/step-size superiority claims in Section 5 and the Conclusions are unsupported; only the error-magnitude comparison is backed by data.
issues.title: Unsupported claim of superior stability/larger admissible steps versus Implicit RK4
issues.why_classification: Rewording to what the tables and analysis actually show preserves the paper's substantive results.
